cim: Financial Times Names Cristina Criddle Chief Artificial Intelligence Correspondent
cim_eredeti: Financial Times Names Cristina Criddle Chief Artificial Intelligence Correspondent
szoveg_eredeti:
The Financial Times has named Cristina Criddle its chief artificial intelligence correspondent, expanding her responsibilities covering one of the technology industry’s fastest-evolving sectors.

Based in San Francisco, Criddle has been with the Financial Times since late 2021, reporting on technology companies and developments shaping the global technology industry.

In her new role, Criddle will focus on artificial intelligence, a sector that has become increasingly important to technology companies, investors, businesses and policymakers worldwide.

Before joining the Financial Times, Criddle worked as a technology reporter at BBC News, covering developments in the technology industry and their broader implications.

Her career at the BBC also included roles as a producer and reporter, giving her experience across broadcast and digital journalism.

Earlier in her career, Criddle worked as a reporter at The Telegraph and held positions at several other major media organizations, including Sky, the Evening Standard, HuffPost and ITV.

She also helped establish The Tab Liverpool in 2012, serving in editorial roles that included editor and features editor.

Criddle is a graduate of the University of Liverpool.

Her appointment comes as news organizations expand their coverage of artificial intelligence, including developments in generative AI, technology industry competition, investment and regulation.

The Financial Times, an international business news organization, covers global financial markets, technology, economics and corporate developments. Criddle’s new position places her at the center of its reporting on the rapidly evolving AI industry.
